correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary triple, cube translation reduces to \(\{\varnothing,A,B\}\). Nested \(A,B\) give a geodesic through the triple. Otherwise the explicit path from \(A\) through \(\varnothing\) to \(B\) deletes \(R=A\cap B\) before \(P=A\setminus B\) and adds \(Q=B\setminus A\) before \(R\). Every nonzero left vertex retains a \(P\)-coordinate and every nonzero right vertex contains a \(Q\)-coordinate, so cross-half pairs differ in at least two coordinates; hence there is no chord. This proves every triple lies on an induced path and therefore \(\operatorname{mp}(Q_n)=2\) for \(n\ge1\). A standalone verifier exhaustively checked all \(388620\) triples through \(Q_7\).

originality.rationale: PASS is limited to the correction claim. The 2020 source explicitly states that the cube has monophonic position number four, while the later Cartesian-product theorem directly entails \(\operatorname{mp}(Q_n)=2\), so the numerical identity is not claimed as standalone novelty. Repeated exact, synonym, hypercube, product-theorem, and correction searches found no indexed source explicitly identifying or repairing this contradiction; the later article does not single out hypercubes in the checked text.

value.rationale: The erroneous cube value is presented in the defining paper as a sharpness witness for a cubic-graph bound. Documenting the contradiction removes a false benchmark, reconciles two pieces of the literature, and supplies a short direct coordinate proof that is independent of the later general product theorem.
